title: Overview
description: What loft does, how your files move between Finder and your storage, and how to run your own installation.

sections.title: More room on your Mac. Your own cloud.
paragraphs: loft is a free, self-hosted drive for macOS. It brings files in your storage into Finder so you can browse them without keeping a full local copy. The menu-bar app handles search, uploads, sharing, and settings.

You run the storage API and choose where the bytes live: a local disk or an S3 bucket. There is no hosted loft account or subscription. This website provides downloads and documentation; it does not store your files.

sections.title: How a file reaches Finder
paragraphs: The Mac client talks to your storage API with an access token. File metadata tells Finder what is available. Opening a file asks the API for its contents, including byte ranges where supported, and the API reads those bytes from your storage.
Keep on This Mac requests a local download for offline use. Those downloaded files consume disk space. A correctly signed File Provider installation is required for the native Finder drive.

sections.title: What you need
paragraphs: Start locally with Bun or Docker, then configure your own server and storage before connecting a remote Mac.
items: macOS 26 or newer for the distributed Mac app; full Xcode 26 or newer when packaging from source.
A server running the Bun storage API, with persistent disk storage or an S3 bucket.
Your own access token and an HTTPS endpoint for remote access.
A self-hosted web build if you want browser management, share landings, or file requests.

sections.title: Hosting and operational costs
paragraphs: loft has no software subscription. You pay your infrastructure provider for storage, compute, and network transfer. The repository’s PolyForm Shield license applies.

The API is designed around one trusted operator and one writer per store. Additional tokens access the same store; they do not create separate user accounts. Back up file data, metadata, sharing records, and configuration.

sections.title: Your API, your address
paragraphs: The local API defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8787. Remote clients must use your server’s address. The public loft website is not an API endpoint.

sections.title: Where to go next
paragraphs: The quick start gets a local server running. Deployment and storage guides cover persistence and remote access; the API reference explains the calls used by the clients.
